body:
Crypto markets opened the week in defensive mode, shedding $2.64 trillion in total market cap as geopolitical tensions and macro uncertainty weighed on risk appetite. The Fear & Greed Index sits firmly in fear territory at 28, barely budging from yesterday's 27, reflecting the cautious sentiment that's gripped traders. Volume remains elevated at $75.3 billion as participants position for what could be a volatile stretch ahead, with BTC dominance holding steady at 58.3% while smaller caps get hammered across the board.

Bitcoin fell 2.11% to $76,707, sliding below the psychological $77,000 level that had provided some technical support last week. The 5.23% weekly decline puts BTC dangerously close to testing the $75,000 support zone, and a break there opens the door to a retest of $70,000. Trump's Iran warning has rattled risk assets globally, and crypto is feeling the pinch alongside equities. Volume at $29.66 billion shows real selling pressure, not just thin orderbook moves. The next 48 hours are critical - hold $75,000 and we might see a bounce, lose it and momentum players will pile on the short side.

Ethereum is getting crushed even harder, down 3.54% to $2,113 as it continues to underperform the broader market with a brutal 9.30% weekly decline. Tom Lee's note about oil-driven ETH selling pressure makes sense given the Middle East tensions, but the real story is the ongoing rotation out of higher-beta alts. Solana fell 3.00% to $84.22, while UNI led the losers board down 4.96% to $3.39. The altcoin complex is showing classic risk-off behavior, with only DOT managing a small 0.07% hourly gain amid the carnage. DeFi tokens are particularly weak as the Verus bridge exploit adds another $11.6 million to the sector's mounting security concerns.

The macro picture is increasingly complex, with Fed minutes looming and oil prices surging on Iran tensions creating a perfect storm for crypto weakness. Reports of Iran considering a Hormuz "insurance" scheme paid in Bitcoin adds an interesting wrinkle, but near-term that's more headline risk than fundamental support. The Senate crypto bill deadline creates another layer of uncertainty, with NYDIG warning the legislation could die if not passed by August. Bitcoin Depot's bankruptcy filing and Kraken's 150-person layoff round out a gloomy news cycle that's feeding the risk-off sentiment.

All eyes turn to Wednesday's Fed minutes and any escalation in Middle East tensions over the next 48 hours. A break below $75,000 in Bitcoin would trigger algorithmic selling and likely push the market into a deeper correction toward $70,000. Conversely, any de-escalation in Iran rhetoric or dovish Fed commentary could spark a relief rally back toward $80,000. The key catalyst remains geopolitical - this market won't find its footing until the Iran situation stabilizes or traders get comfortable pricing in the risk premium.
